title: StealthRL: Reinforcement Learning Paraphrase Attacks for Multi-Detector Evasion of AI-Text Detectors
abstract: arXiv:2602.08934v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: AI-text detectors are increasingly used in high-stakes settings, but their robustness to meaning-preserving adversarial rewriting remains unclear. We introduce StealthRL, a reinforcement learning framework for stress-testing detectors with adaptive paraphrase attacks. StealthRL trains a paraphrase policy against a detector ensemble while enforcing semantic fidelity, then evaluates transfer to held-out detector families on the full filtered MAGE test pool. Across RoBERTa, Fast-DetectGPT, Binoculars, and MAGE, the resulting attack sharply degrades detection performance, driving mean TPR@1%FPR down to 0.024 while retaining nontrivial semantic overlap and readable prose. The attack also transfers to detectors not used during training, indicating a broader robustness failure rather than overfitting to a single target model. translated_title: StealthRL：用于规避多种AI文本检测器的强化学习改写攻击
translated_abstract: AI文本检测器越来越多地被应用于高风险场景，但它们对保持语义不变的对抗性改写的鲁棒性仍不明确。我们提出了StealthRL，一个利用自适应改写攻击对检测器进行压力测试的强化学习框架。StealthRL在强制保持语义保真度的同时，针对一个检测器集成训练改写策略，随后在完整的过滤MAGE测试集上评估其对未参与训练的检测器家族的迁移能力。在RoBERTa、Fast-DetectGPT、Binoculars和MAGE等检测器上，该攻击显著降低了检测性能，将平均TPR@1%FPR降至0.024，同时保留了可观的语义重叠度和流畅可读的文本。该攻击还能迁移到训练中未使用过的检测器，表明这反映的是更广泛的鲁棒性缺陷，而非对单一目标模型的过拟合。我们还通过检测器得分分析、重复生成稳定性检验和自动化（评估）对主要结果进行了补充。
tldr: 本文提出StealthRL强化学习改写攻击框架，在保持语义保真度和文本可读性的前提下，将多种AI文本检测器的平均TPR@1%FPR降至0.024，且攻击可迁移至训练中未见的检测器，揭示了AI文本检测器普遍存在的鲁棒性缺陷。
en_tdlr: StealthRL is a reinforcement learning paraphrase attack framework that sharply degrades multiple AI-text detectors (mean TPR@1%FPR drops to 0.024) while preserving semantic fidelity and readability, and transfers to unseen detectors, revealing a broad robustness failure of AI-text detection.
